## Purpose

This report demonstrates how I would structure an observational program evaluation when participation is not randomly assigned. The data are synthetic; the design choices and diagnostic sequence mirror a real evaluation workflow.

## Analysis sequence

~~~{r}
#| label: run-analysis
source("../R/01_generate_synthetic_data.R")
source("../R/02_estimate_effects.R")
source("../R/03_diagnostics.R")
~~~

## Covariate balance

~~~{r}
#| label: balance-results
balance <- readr::read_csv(
  "../outputs/balance_table.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(balance, digits = 3)
~~~

Balance is assessed using absolute standardized mean differences, with 0.10 used as a diagnostic threshold rather than a mechanical guarantee of exchangeability.

## Effect estimates

~~~{r}
#| label: effect-results
effects <- readr::read_csv(
  "../outputs/effect_estimates.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(effects, digits = 3)
~~~

Agreement across matched, weighted, and regression-adjusted estimates is treated as a robustness signal. It does not resolve possible bias from unmeasured confounders.

## What I would add with real data

A production evaluation would add a missing-data plan, attrition analysis, outcome specification checks, sensitivity analysis for unmeasured confounding, subgroup estimates defined before modeling, and a data-provenance appendix.
